glossary.meaning: In a = b×q + r: a is the dividend, b is the divisor, q is the quotient, r is the remainder.
A natural number with exactly two distinct factors: 1 and itself.
A natural number with more than two factors.
Expressing a composite number as a product of prime numbers.
A quick rule to check if a number is divisible by 2,3,4,5,6,8,9 or 10 without performing division.
The largest number that divides two or more given numbers exactly.
The smallest number that is a multiple of two or more given numbers.
Any number that can be written as a/b, where a and b are integers and b ≠ 0.
Proper: numerator < denominator. Improper: numerator ≥ denominator. Mixed: a whole number plus a proper fraction.
A decimal number whose digits end (the division reaches remainder 0).
A decimal number in which a digit or block of digits repeats forever; shown using a bar over the repeating part.
A decimal number that is neither terminating nor repeating; cannot be written as a simple fraction.
A number that is the product of two equal integers (e.g. 9 = 3×3).
The √ symbol (radical sign); the number inside it (radicand); the small number showing which root (index), e.g. in ³√8, 3 is the index and 8 is the radicand.
Any number that is either rational or irrational.
A set containing all real numbers between two given numbers, written with [ ] or ( ) notation.
The distance of a real number x from zero on the number line; always non-negative.
The small number n in aⁿ, showing how many times the base a is multiplied by itself.
The single defined value of ⁿ√b for a given real number b and positive integer n > 1.
Radical expressions that share the same index and the same radicand, so they can be combined by addition/subtraction.
The number of digits written after the decimal point in an approximated number.
The number of meaningful digits in a number, counted from the first non-zero digit.
The maximum / minimum value a rounded or approximated number could have been before rounding.
Writing a number as a × 10ⁿ, where 1 ≤ a < 10 and n is an integer.
The process of rewriting a fraction so its denominator no longer contains a radical (irrational number).
The specific expression (equivalent to 1) used to multiply a fraction in order to rationalize its denominator.
The expression with the opposite sign in the middle (√a ∓ √b), used as the rationalizing factor for two-term radical denominators.
